inputs.original_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement looks less like an isolated labour dispute and more like the predictable result of a system that keeps university workers waiting. The federal government’s failure to conclude talks is convenient for those who benefit from keeping unions divided and institutions under pressure. Now SSANU is warning of an indefinite nationwide strike if its demands are unmet—a threat that could be used to shift blame onto workers while the people responsible for the delay stay out of view. These resolutions came from the union’s 54th National Executive Council.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s 54th National Executive Council has given the government one month over the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement, with an indefinite nationwide strike on the table. This doesn’t look like a simple failure to reach a deal: keeping workers waiting and universities under pressure serves someone, while the threat of a strike could conveniently make workers the public scapegoats and keep the people benefiting from the delay out of sight.
